candidate_digest_recipe: git ls-files plus git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, sorted; sha256 over, for each path in order, the UTF-8 path bytes followed by the RAW 32-byte sha256 digest (not its hex text) of the file content. This manifest IS included. Its contribution is the sha256 of json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) with ONLY THE FIELD BEING COMPUTED blanked to the empty string - that one field at the top level and in every acceptance_rounds entry. The other digest keeps its real value. Computing tested_candidate_digest blanks tested_candidate_digest alone; evidence_bundle_digest is still empty at that point, so nothing is lost. Computing evidence_bundle_digest blanks evidence_bundle_digest alone; tested_candidate_digest is already frozen, so the evidence digest depends on it. That dependency IS the binding between the evidence and the input the acceptance streams judged. An earlier form blanked BOTH fields, on the stated rationale that naming a single field would be self-referentially impossible once the second field held a value. That rationale was wrong: each field is computed at a moment when the other is either empty or already frozen, so both directions are deterministic. The consequence was measured, not argued - under blank-both, three different tested_candidate_digest values produced one identical evidence digest, so the field naming which tree was judged could hold any 64-hex string forever while every check stayed silent. Found by independent review, at exactly the place the surrounding prose claimed a binding the arithmetic could not provide.

digest_model.tested_candidate_digest: Frozen BEFORE the acceptance streams start. It identifies the immutable input they judge. Recorded here once the streams are dispatched and never edited afterwards; if it must change, the round is void and a new one begins.
digest_model.evidence_bundle_digest: Computed AFTER the results are written. It identifies the tree that carries the acceptance evidence. It necessarily differs from tested_candidate_digest, because writing PASS into the tree changes the tree.
digest_model.why_split: An earlier form recorded one digest, computed after the acceptance records were written. It therefore identified the post-acceptance evidence tree rather than the input the streams actually judged - the acceptance appeared to certify a tree that did not exist when it ran. Found by independent review.
digest_model.artifact_manifest_sha256: Unrelated to both. It certifies the four reviewed families unchanged and is deliberately invariant across rebuilds that leave the contracts alone.
digest_model.round_scoped: Both digests are recorded twice: at the top level for the current round, and inside the matching acceptance_rounds entry as history. Without the per-round copy a retro-edit of the top-level value and a genuine new round would be indistinguishable, so 'frozen and never edited afterwards' would not be checkable. Named by the QA author, who declined to write a test asserting a property the structure could not support.
digest_model.every_aggregate_names_its_commit: The rule this manifest now keeps, and the one it asserted before it kept it. Every aggregate here names the commit it was computed over, or states 'this file's own commit' where a commit cannot name its own hash. tested_candidate_digest is bound per round by candidate_frozen_at_commit - all six rounds that carry a digest, 5 to 10 - and evidence_bundle_digest by evidence_bundle_commit, which is the RATIFICATION commit and not the freeze commit, because the evidence is written after the freeze by construction. Each recovered value was resolved by running the manifest's own recipe over every revision of this file on any ref and taking the one it reproduces at, never from prose.

recorded_limits.evidence_report_visibility: The acceptance digests enumerate git ls-files --exclude-standard, so a report path added to .gitignore leaves the digest and every check silent about its content - an independent reviewer demonstrated a fabricated manual report passing that way. It is a declared scope limit rather than a hidden hole: the attack requires editing .gitignore, which is tracked and inside the digest, so it appears in the diff a reviewer reads. The next task touching the QA module must assert that both report paths are tracked and not ignored; it is not opened as its own round because the current mechanism makes the manoeuvre visible rather than invisible.
recorded_limits.prefix_widening_unpinned: ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_PREFIX and RATIFIABLE_REVIEWED_PREFIX are unpinned in the widening direction only; the guarantee is that report paths are confined to some declared prefix, not that the prefix is the narrow one. recorded_limits.state_record_sweep: artifacts/checkpoints/CP-00/check_state_records.py is the completeness check for two axes: a superseded QA evidence commit presented as current, and stale round accounting - which acceptance round is owed, and how many are in the record. Both are bound to the structural unit containing an occurrence - the enclosing JSON object or string value under its key trail, the enclosing table row, or the enclosing sentence - not to a line window, because a window is proximity rather than attribution and the earlier form exited 0 on the very tree it was written for. The round-accounting axis derives its truth from current_round and acceptance_rounds in this manifest instead of restating them, so the sweep cannot itself go stale; four records must state both claims in a form the check can read, so a document that says nothing does not pass for the wrong reason; and nothing is skipped by path except the dated primary acceptance reports and the checker itself. Both axes are measured rather than asserted: --rev sweeps any commit's objects without a checkout, and the axis-one findings at bde3af3, a3eaf88 and 5b70ee4 are 1, 1 and 4. --selftest proves each axis-two detector fires and that a history label excuses only the unit containing it. Limits: it checks the owed round and the round count, not each round's recorded verdict; and a claim inside a per-round entry or an object carrying superseded_by is treated as dated history and not swept.
